findings.title: react/no-danger set to "warn" contradicts "fail loudly" claim
findings.desc: The block's comment states these rules are "guardrails that fail loudly if a future change tries to weaken" the XSS defenses, but `react/no-danger` is configured as `"warn"` rather than `"error"`. Unless the lint script treats warnings as failures, a future introduction of `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` would not actually fail CI, contradicting the stated intent.

findings.title: no-restricted-imports only catches static ES import of rehype-raw
findings.desc: The `no-restricted-imports` rule targets `ImportDeclaration`s named `rehype-raw`; it will not flag `require('rehype-raw')` or dynamic `import('rehype-raw')`, leaving a gap in the "defense-in-depth" guardrail it claims to provide.
